- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Handoff — Tablet/Desktop merchant app (branch `feat/tablet-desktop-app`)
2	
3	Date: 2026-07-28, updated 2026-08-07
4	Status: **implementation and headless acceptance complete** — all 15 screens, the
5	§9 accepted-change queue, P5 tutorial adaptation, the Trades refinements, and P6
6	browser/automated QA are committed or ready in the final QA commit. See
7	`docs/VERIFY-2026-08-07-tablet-desktop-final-qa.md` for the recorded checks and the
8	two remaining external manual gates (real-device push and a staging Windcave flow).
9	
10	> **If you are picking this up cold and about to work on the terminal's "no
11	> payment board" option, read `docs/PLAN-2026-08-06-payment-links-no-board.md`
12	> first.** The corrected token flow and Phase 0 safety foundation are implemented
13	> and verified against an isolated PostgreSQL 16 database. Production rollout is
14	> still gated by the migration/deployment sequence and the external smoke checks
15	> recorded in the final QA report.
16	Read `docs/PLAN-2026-07-24-tablet-desktop-app.md` first: it is still the authoritative
17	spec for scope, device gating, routes and per-screen requirements. This file records
18	what has actually been built, the conventions to follow, the traps that have already
19	cost time, and what to do next.
20	
21	---
22	
23	## 1. Where things stand
24	
25	| Screen | Route | File | Commit |
26	|---|---|---|---|

43	
44	P5 and P6 are complete in code and headless/browser verification. No screen is a
45	stub — every `client/src/desktop/pages/*.tsx` renders a real screen. The remaining
46	work is review, the external manual gates, and controlled deployment.
47	
48	Deliberately left out of finished screens, each worth its own pass rather than a
49	cramped port: co-tenants on the add-tenant form (2b), attach-invoice upload plus
50	the split toggle on a bill (2c), and the split toggle on a job invoice (3c).
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 2. How to build a screen (the loop that has worked)
55	
56	1. **Read the design markup for that screen** in
57	   `docs/design/desktop-app/Taptpay Desktop.dc.html`. Screen offsets:
58	   retail 4a–4e at lines 40 / 233 / 302 / 526 / 766; property 2a–2e at
59	   1710 / 1947 / 2001 / 2217 / 2494; trades 3a–3e at 883 / 1076 / 1130 / 1354 / 1593.
60	   The rendered targets are `docs/design/desktop-app/screens/dt--*.png`.
61	2. **Read the prototype's logic** for that screen — the `<script type="text/x-dc">`
62	   block (~line 2621+). Property state atoms are unprefixed, trades are `tr*`,
63	   retail are `rt*`. That map is the interaction spec: what toggles, what animates,
64	   what a button does.
65	3. **Find the mobile page that owns the same logic** and reuse its endpoints,
66	   mutations and validation. Never invent an endpoint; never re-derive a fee or a
67	   GST rate that already exists in `lib/report-utils.ts`.
68	4. **Verify against the schema, not against the mobile page's variable names.**
69	   See §4 — three field-name assumptions have already been wrong.
70	5. Write the page as a single file with a page-scoped CSS template literal (class
71	   prefix per page: `rh-`, `rs-`, `rt-`, `ra-`, `ds-`, `ph-`). This matches the
72	   codebase's per-vertical-page convention.
73	6. **Verify** (§5), then commit that one screen with a message that states what was
74	   wired and what deviates from the design.
75	
76	### Layout conventions
77	
78	- The canvas is exactly **1180×880**. `DesktopShell` renders a 66px header + 1px
79	  divider, then `.tapt-desktop-main` (1180×813, `position: relative`) holding your
80	  page. So a design coordinate `y` inside a screen maps to `y - 66` in your page.
81	- The design's own absolute offsets can be ported verbatim once you subtract that
82	  66 (and the body padding, if your container has any). 4c's rail and 4d's report
83	  blocks do exactly this and match the PNGs.
84	- Pass `showScope={false}` to `DesktopPageScaffold` when the screen draws its own
85	  scope control inside a column (every content page does).
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 3. Verification (do all of it before committing)
90	
91	```bash
92	npx tsc --noEmit                    # must be silent
93	npx vite build                      # each desktop page must land in its own chunk
94	node scripts/verify-desktop-p0.mjs  # device gating, frame geometry, chunk isolation, tutorial spotlight
95	npx jest client/src/pages/__tests__/smoke-tests.test.tsx client/src/__tests__/tutorial-registry.test.ts
96	```
97	
98	Then **screenshot the screen you built at both device classes** and compare with the
99	design PNG. Working examples live in `scripts/desktop-shots/` — copy the closest one,
100	swap the route and fixtures:
101	
102	```bash
103	node scripts/desktop-shots/shot-property-home.mjs   # → /tmp/taptpay-desktop-2a/*.png
104	node scripts/desktop-shots/shot-trades-terminal.mjs # → /tmp/taptpay-desktop-3c/*.png
105	```
106	
107	The five trades scripts share `scripts/desktop-shots/trades-fixtures.mjs` — clients,
108	quotes, invoices, the API mocks, a frozen clock, and `newTradesPage`/`runTradesShots`.
109	Use it for further trades work rather than re-inventing fixtures; a screen needing an
110	extra row registers its own `page.route` afterwards, because Playwright matches the
111	most recently registered route first.
112	
113	Those scripts encode the things that are easy to get wrong:
114	
115	- Chromium must be the nix one:
116	  `/nix/store/zi4f80l169xlmivz8vja8wlphq74qqk0-chromium-125.0.6422.141/bin/chromium`
117	  (the bundled Playwright browser is broken — see memory `playwright-nix-chromium`).
118	- Auth is a **dummy JWT written to `localStorage` in an init script** plus
119	  `page.route` mocks; no server data is needed.
120	- **Desktop** = `{ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } }` → centred 13″ frame.
121	  **Tablet** = `{ viewport: { width: 1194, height: 834 }, hasTouch: true }` → full
122	  bleed. Without `hasTouch` the pointer is fine and you get the desktop path, so you
123	  are not actually testing the tablet.
124	- Assert `no page errors`. Several scripts currently collect/print errors but still
125	  exit zero; the corrected payment plan Phase 1/6 requires hard failure before those
126	  scripts count as a gate.
127	
128	The dev server must already be running on **:5000, single instance only** (memory
129	`dev-server-single-instance`); the workflow does not auto-restart.
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 4. Traps that have already cost time
134	
135	**Verify field names in `shared/schema.ts` before writing any aggregation.**
136	
137	- Retail transactions: `price` (decimal string), `taptStoneId`, `splitEnabled`,
138	  `totalRefunded`, `refundableAmount`, `paymentMethod`. Clients currently send the
139	  request-only `selectedStoneId`; MemStorage maps it, but production DatabaseStorage
140	  does not until the corrected plan's Phase 0 canonical input is implemented.
141	- **There is no merchant-level split flag.** `splitEnabled` is a column on
142	  *transactions*. Gating split UI on `merchant.splitEnabled` hides it forever.
143	- Rent invoices (`invoices_rent_requests`): **`amountCents` (integer cents)** and
144	  **`dueAt`** — not `amount`/`dueDate`. Voided status is **`"voided"`**.
145	- Tenants (`tenant_profiles`): **`firstName` + `lastName`**, no `name` field.
146	- Schedules (`active_schedules`): `amountCents`, `frequency`, `nextRunDate`.
147	- Payment links come from the server: `merchant.paymentUrl`, `merchant.qrCodeUrl`,
148	  and per-board `stone.paymentUrl`. Do not hand-build `${origin}/pay/:id` (that is
149	  only payment-stack's fallback).
150	
151	**Trades invoices are not free-form.** `createJobInvoiceSchema` refuses a `deposit`
152	that is not linked to a quote, and a `balance` is issued by the server from an
153	already-paid deposit (`POST /api/trades/invoices/:id/send-balance`, amount computed
154	from the quote total) rather than composed on the client. 3c's three type chips are
155	therefore three different operations, two of them conditionally disabled. Quote GST
156	comes from `@shared/trades-gst`'s `computeQuoteTotals` with the merchant's
157	`gstRegistered`/`tradeGstMode`; the fee is `tradesFeeCents` in `lib/trades-money.ts`.
158	
159	**Property data must go through `client/src/lib/property-data.ts`** hooks
160	(`usePropertyTenants` / `usePropertyInvoices` / `usePropertySchedules`). That file
161	says MUST, and it is how mutations invalidate every consumer at once.
162	
163	**Pointer drags must be divided by the canvas scale.** The canvas is
164	`transform: scale(...)`; pointer deltas arrive in viewport pixels. Read the scale off
165	the nearest `[data-desktop-scale]` ancestor and divide, or the element lags the
166	cursor on desktop. 4d's sheet is the reference implementation.
167	
168	**Billing gate is free if you use `apiRequest`** — a 402 `BILLING_CARD_REQUIRED`
169	dispatches a global event that `NotificationProvider` already renders.
170	
171	**Don't trust the prototype's numbers.** Every hard-coded row in the design file is a
172	placeholder. If a figure has no data behind it, leave it out and say so — see §6.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. Reusable pieces already built
177	
178	- `desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.tsx` — the **shared** settings screen. 2e and 3e are
179	  two-line wrappers: `<DesktopSettingsPage {...props} vertical="property" />`.
180	- `desktop/data/retail-reports.ts` — pure report engine (10 retail reports).
181	  `property-reports.ts` (4) and `trades-reports.ts` (4) follow the same shape: a
182	  metadata array + one `build*Report(id, ctx)` switch returning
183	  `{heroV, h2V, chart, segs|bars, rows}`. Property and trades expose only the
184	  reports that have a real PDF implementation — design tiles with no backing data
185	  were dropped, not mocked.
186	- `desktop/data/trades-data.ts` — the trades cache and domain layer (query hooks on
187	  the mobile keys, `scopeTradesData`, `buildTradesClientRows`, `buildTradesHealth`,
188	  period/bucket helpers). Every trades screen reads through it, which is why a
189	  client's status is identical on home, directory and terminal.
190	- `desktop/data/desktop-prefs.ts` — per-merchant localStorage preferences.
191	- `hooks/use-push-notifications.ts` — web + native-iOS push subscribe/unsubscribe.
192	- `lib/report-utils.ts` — money, NZ GST, timeframe windows. Use these, don't re-derive.
193	- `lib/property-dashboard-data.ts` — `periodWindow`, `buildBuckets`, `collectedCents`,
194	  `growthPct`, `filterByProperty`. Retail adapts transactions into the invoice shape
195	  these expect (see the top of `retail-home.tsx`'s model) so both verticals bucket
196	  identically.
197	
198	Not yet extracted: the home-screen furniture (bar chart, health strip, entity list,
199	quick actions) is duplicated between `retail-home.tsx` (`rh-`) and `property-home.tsx`
200	(`ph-`). The plan wants it extracted; trades home is the third call site and the
201	sensible moment. Treat it as a decision, not an oversight.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## 6. Deviations — RAISED AND RULED ON (2026-08-06)
206	
207	The full list was put to Oliver on 2026-08-06 and he ruled on every item. **Do not
208	re-raise these.** Rulings below; the accepted-change queue is §9.
209	
210	**Shipped as fixes** (committed 2026-08-06):
211	
212	| Item | Ruling | Commit |
213	|---|---|---|
214	| 4d/3d peak dot floating in the fill | fix it | `4ade651` |
215	| 2b vs 3b hero count contradiction | make 2b match 3b | `5cadc4d` |
216	| 4c keypad `.`/`<` keys | centre both as glyphs, not characters | `6067bd4` |

# Handoff — Tablet/Desktop merchant app (branch `feat/tablet-desktop-app`)

Date: 2026-07-28, updated 2026-08-07
Status: **implementation and headless acceptance complete** — all 15 screens, the
§9 accepted-change queue, P5 tutorial adaptation, the Trades refinements, and P6
browser/automated QA are committed or ready in the final QA commit. See
`docs/VERIFY-2026-08-07-tablet-desktop-final-qa.md` for the recorded checks and the
two remaining external manual gates (real-device push and a staging Windcave flow).

> **If you are picking this up cold and about to work on the terminal's "no
> payment board" option, read `docs/PLAN-2026-08-06-payment-links-no-board.md`
> first.** The corrected token flow and Phase 0 safety foundation are implemented
> and verified against an isolated PostgreSQL 16 database. Production rollout is
> still gated by the migration/deployment sequence and the external smoke checks
> recorded in the final QA report.
Read `docs/PLAN-2026-07-24-tablet-desktop-app.md` first: it is still the authoritative
spec for scope, device gating, routes and per-screen requirements. This file records
what has actually been built, the conventions to follow, the traps that have already
cost time, and what to do next.

---

## 1. Where things stand

| Screen | Route | File | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 scaffold | — | `client/src/desktop/{DesktopFrame,ScaledCanvas,DesktopShell,DesktopPageScaffold,desktop-theme,desktop.css}` | `58ba709` |
| 4a retail home | `/dashboard` | `desktop/pages/retail-home.tsx` | `60118b5` |
| 4b retail stock | `/stock` | `desktop/pages/retail-stock.tsx` | `87146de` |
| 4c retail terminal | `/terminal` | `desktop/pages/retail-terminal.tsx` | `525b302` |
| 4d retail analytics | `/transactions` | `desktop/pages/retail-analytics.tsx` + `desktop/data/retail-reports.ts` | `91865d6` |
| 4e settings (all verticals) | `/settings` | `desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.tsx` + `desktop/pages/retail-settings.tsx` | `a81c04a` |
| 2a property home | `/property` | `desktop/pages/property-home.tsx` | `dc8f2b9` |
| 2b property clients | `/property/tenants` | `desktop/pages/property-clients.tsx` | `10405a0` |
| 2c property terminal | `/property/terminal` | `desktop/pages/property-terminal.tsx` | `3e3b6c6` |
| 2d property analytics | `/property/analytics` | `desktop/pages/property-analytics.tsx` + `desktop/data/property-reports.ts` | `912c1e7` |
| 2e property settings | `/settings` | `desktop/pages/property-settings.tsx` (wrapper) | `79b5dcc` |
| 3a trades home | `/trades` | `desktop/pages/trades-home.tsx` + `desktop/data/trades-data.ts` | `934442b` |
| 3b trades clients | `/trades/clients` | `desktop/pages/trades-clients.tsx` | `2f0101a` |
| 3c trades terminal | `/trades/terminal` | `desktop/pages/trades-terminal.tsx` | `ba37025` |
| 3d trades analytics | `/trades/analytics` | `desktop/pages/trades-analytics.tsx` + `desktop/data/trades-reports.ts` | `404fbaa` |
| 3e trades settings | `/settings` | `desktop/pages/trades-settings.tsx` (wrapper) | `812e21d` |

P5 and P6 are complete in code and headless/browser verification. No screen is a
stub — every `client/src/desktop/pages/*.tsx` renders a real screen. The remaining
work is review, the external manual gates, and controlled deployment.

Deliberately left out of finished screens, each worth its own pass rather than a
cramped port: co-tenants on the add-tenant form (2b), attach-invoice upload plus
the split toggle on a bill (2c), and the split toggle on a job invoice (3c).

---

## 2. How to build a screen (the loop that has worked)

1. **Read the design markup for that screen** in
   `docs/design/desktop-app/Taptpay Desktop.dc.html`. Screen offsets:
   retail 4a–4e at lines 40 / 233 / 302 / 526 / 766; property 2a–2e at
   1710 / 1947 / 2001 / 2217 / 2494; trades 3a–3e at 883 / 1076 / 1130 / 1354 / 1593.
   The rendered targets are `docs/design/desktop-app/screens/dt--*.png`.
2. **Read the prototype's logic** for that screen — the `<script type="text/x-dc">`
   block (~line 2621+). Property state atoms are unprefixed, trades are `tr*`,
   retail are `rt*`. That map is the interaction spec: what toggles, what animates,
   what a button does.
3. **Find the mobile page that owns the same logic** and reuse its endpoints,
   mutations and validation. Never invent an endpoint; never re-derive a fee or a
   GST rate that already exists in `lib/report-utils.ts`.
4. **Verify against the schema, not against the mobile page's variable names.**
   See §4 — three field-name assumptions have already been wrong.
5. Write the page as a single file with a page-scoped CSS template literal (class
   prefix per page: `rh-`, `rs-`, `rt-`, `ra-`, `ds-`, `ph-`). This matches the
   codebase's per-vertical-page convention.
6. **Verify** (§5), then commit that one screen with a message that states what was
   wired and what deviates from the design.

### Layout conventions

- The canvas is exactly **1180×880**. `DesktopShell` renders a 66px header + 1px
  divider, then `.tapt-desktop-main` (1180×813, `position: relative`) holding your
  page. So a design coordinate `y` inside a screen maps to `y - 66` in your page.
- The design's own absolute offsets can be ported verbatim once you subtract that
  66 (and the body padding, if your container has any). 4c's rail and 4d's report
  blocks do exactly this and match the PNGs.
- Pass `showScope={false}` to `DesktopPageScaffold` when the screen draws its own
  scope control inside a column (every content page does).

---

## 3. Verification (do all of it before committing)

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit                    # must be silent
npx vite build                      # each desktop page must land in its own chunk
node scripts/verify-desktop-p0.mjs  # device gating, frame geometry, chunk isolation, tutorial spotlight
npx jest client/src/pages/__tests__/smoke-tests.test.tsx client/src/__tests__/tutorial-registry.test.ts
```

Then **screenshot the screen you built at both device classes** and compare with the
design PNG. Working examples live in `scripts/desktop-shots/` — copy the closest one,
swap the route and fixtures:

```bash
node scripts/desktop-shots/shot-property-home.mjs   # → /tmp/taptpay-desktop-2a/*.png
node scripts/desktop-shots/shot-trades-terminal.mjs # → /tmp/taptpay-desktop-3c/*.png
```

The five trades scripts share `scripts/desktop-shots/trades-fixtures.mjs` — clients,
quotes, invoices, the API mocks, a frozen clock, and `newTradesPage`/`runTradesShots`.
Use it for further trades work rather than re-inventing fixtures; a screen needing an
extra row registers its own `page.route` afterwards, because Playwright matches the
most recently registered route first.

Those scripts encode the things that are easy to get wrong:

- Chromium must be the nix one:
  `/nix/store/zi4f80l169xlmivz8vja8wlphq74qqk0-chromium-125.0.6422.141/bin/chromium`
  (the bundled Playwright browser is broken — see memory `playwright-nix-chromium`).
- Auth is a **dummy JWT written to `localStorage` in an init script** plus
  `page.route` mocks; no server data is needed.
- **Desktop** = `{ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } }` → centred 13″ frame.
  **Tablet** = `{ viewport: { width: 1194, height: 834 }, hasTouch: true }` → full
  bleed. Without `hasTouch` the pointer is fine and you get the desktop path, so you
  are not actually testing the tablet.
- Assert `no page errors`. Several scripts currently collect/print errors but still
  exit zero; the corrected payment plan Phase 1/6 requires hard failure before those
  scripts count as a gate.

The dev server must already be running on **:5000, single instance only** (memory
`dev-server-single-instance`); the workflow does not auto-restart.

---

## 4. Traps that have already cost time

**Verify field names in `shared/schema.ts` before writing any aggregation.**

- Retail transactions: `price` (decimal string), `taptStoneId`, `splitEnabled`,
  `totalRefunded`, `refundableAmount`, `paymentMethod`. Clients currently send the
  request-only `selectedStoneId`; MemStorage maps it, but production DatabaseStorage
  does not until the corrected plan's Phase 0 canonical input is implemented.
- **There is no merchant-level split flag.** `splitEnabled` is a column on
  *transactions*. Gating split UI on `merchant.splitEnabled` hides it forever.
- Rent invoices (`invoices_rent_requests`): **`amountCents` (integer cents)** and
  **`dueAt`** — not `amount`/`dueDate`. Voided status is **`"voided"`**.
- Tenants (`tenant_profiles`): **`firstName` + `lastName`**, no `name` field.
- Schedules (`active_schedules`): `amountCents`, `frequency`, `nextRunDate`.
- Payment links come from the server: `merchant.paymentUrl`, `merchant.qrCodeUrl`,
  and per-board `stone.paymentUrl`. Do not hand-build `${origin}/pay/:id` (that is
  only payment-stack's fallback).

**Trades invoices are not free-form.** `createJobInvoiceSchema` refuses a `deposit`
that is not linked to a quote, and a `balance` is issued by the server from an
already-paid deposit (`POST /api/trades/invoices/:id/send-balance`, amount computed
from the quote total) rather than composed on the client. 3c's three type chips are
therefore three different operations, two of them conditionally disabled. Quote GST
comes from `@shared/trades-gst`'s `computeQuoteTotals` with the merchant's
`gstRegistered`/`tradeGstMode`; the fee is `tradesFeeCents` in `lib/trades-money.ts`.

**Property data must go through `client/src/lib/property-data.ts`** hooks
(`usePropertyTenants` / `usePropertyInvoices` / `usePropertySchedules`). That file
says MUST, and it is how mutations invalidate every consumer at once.

**Pointer drags must be divided by the canvas scale.** The canvas is
`transform: scale(...)`; pointer deltas arrive in viewport pixels. Read the scale off
the nearest `[data-desktop-scale]` ancestor and divide, or the element lags the
cursor on desktop. 4d's sheet is the reference implementation.

**Billing gate is free if you use `apiRequest`** — a 402 `BILLING_CARD_REQUIRED`
dispatches a global event that `NotificationProvider` already renders.

**Don't trust the prototype's numbers.** Every hard-coded row in the design file is a
placeholder. If a figure has no data behind it, leave it out and say so — see §6.

---

## 5. Reusable pieces already built

- `desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.tsx` — the **shared** settings screen. 2e and 3e are
  two-line wrappers: `<DesktopSettingsPage {...props} vertical="property" />`.
- `desktop/data/retail-reports.ts` — pure report engine (10 retail reports).
  `property-reports.ts` (4) and `trades-reports.ts` (4) follow the same shape: a
  metadata array + one `build*Report(id, ctx)` switch returning
  `{heroV, h2V, chart, segs|bars, rows}`. Property and trades expose only the
  reports that have a real PDF implementation — design tiles with no backing data
  were dropped, not mocked.
- `desktop/data/trades-data.ts` — the trades cache and domain layer (query hooks on
  the mobile keys, `scopeTradesData`, `buildTradesClientRows`, `buildTradesHealth`,
  period/bucket helpers). Every trades screen reads through it, which is why a
  client's status is identical on home, directory and terminal.
- `desktop/data/desktop-prefs.ts` — per-merchant localStorage preferences.
- `hooks/use-push-notifications.ts` — web + native-iOS push subscribe/unsubscribe.
- `lib/report-utils.ts` — money, NZ GST, timeframe windows. Use these, don't re-derive.
- `lib/property-dashboard-data.ts` — `periodWindow`, `buildBuckets`, `collectedCents`,
  `growthPct`, `filterByProperty`. Retail adapts transactions into the invoice shape
  these expect (see the top of `retail-home.tsx`'s model) so both verticals bucket
  identically.

Not yet extracted: the home-screen furniture (bar chart, health strip, entity list,
quick actions) is duplicated between `retail-home.tsx` (`rh-`) and `property-home.tsx`
(`ph-`). The plan wants it extracted; trades home is the third call site and the
sensible moment. Treat it as a decision, not an oversight.

---

## 6. Deviations — RAISED AND RULED ON (2026-08-06)

The full list was put to Oliver on 2026-08-06 and he ruled on every item. **Do not
re-raise these.** Rulings below; the accepted-change queue is §9.

**Shipped as fixes** (committed 2026-08-06):

### Transitions/cascade deviations — RULED 2026-08-08

Raised as a single list once the page-transition integration finished (`666b898`
+ `a7d15a3`). Oliver ruled **keep all four as shipped**. Do not re-raise these,
and do not "fix" them — each is load-bearing.

| Kept as shipped | Because |
|---|---|
| Drag sheets (`.ra-sheet`/`.pa-sheet`/`.ta-sheet`) are excluded from the cascade; their contents pop in, the sheet shell does not | The sheets carry a live inline `transform: translateY(...)` for dragging, and a `both`-filled keyframe pins them at `translateY(0)`, breaking the drag |
| `.pa-dot` chart peak marker does not pop in | It is centred by `transform: translate(-50%,-50%)`, which a cascade transform displaces. Independent of the already-ruled dot *position* fix (`4ade651`) |
| Rails animate on `.rt-rail`/`.pt-rail`/`.tt-rail` themselves, never their slots — so rails do not stagger internally | A transform on a slot makes that slot the containing block for the `position:absolute` rail, moving the rail |
| The property/trades analytics overview replays its cascade when a generated report is closed | The overview sits inside `{!report && …}`. Gating it is cheap if it ever grates |

### Closed 2026-08-09

Everything left open on that list is now done except the visual side-by-side.

**`probe-transitions.mjs` is a usable gate — it exits 0 on a healthy tree.** It
used to log a "loader flash" for any added `.animate-spin` node, catching
`/board-builder`'s own content spinners. It now separates three signals, and only
the first two decide the exit code:

| Signal | Meaning | Gates? |
|---|---|---|
| chrome `REMOUNTED` | the frame was torn down and rebuilt | yes |
| `route-loader` | `[data-testid='page-loader']`, the full-screen loader, painted over the app | yes |
| page-slot suspension / content spinner | chrome held; a page showed its own loading state | reported only |

Desktop routes cannot render the route loader at all — their fallback is the
deliberately empty `DesktopPageFallback`, which now carries
`data-testid='desktop-page-fallback'` so a suspended page slot can be *timed*
rather than confused with a flash. Current run, both device classes:
**0/21 chrome remounts, 0 route-loader flashes**, 14 page-slot suspensions
(worst ~130ms) and 1 content spinner, all informational.

**Cascade coverage is audited, by a new probe.** `scripts/desktop-shots/probe-cascade.mjs`
samples `document.getAnimations()` right after each hop and reports how many
elements actually run `desktopBounceIn` and how deep the stagger goes. Two things
fail it: a screen that cascades nothing, and — the expensive one — an element
carrying `.dt-rise`/`.dt-cascade > *` that settles at opacity 0. The rule ships
`opacity: 0` under an `animation: … both` fill, so a block whose animation never
runs is not merely un-animated, it is *permanently invisible*, and nothing else
in the suite would catch that. Result: **13/13 screens on both desktop and
tablet**, every one genuinely staggered (4–12 steps at the 52ms interval), zero
stuck invisible.

**The six empty CSS declarations at `trades-terminal.tsx:1224-1229` are filled.**
They were the quick-invoice recipient block's `color:`/`background:` with the
values dropped. The file's own convention settles what they should be — pressed
chip = `ACTIVE` background + `NAVY` text, unpressed = `ACCENT_SOFT` on
transparent (see the inline styles at lines 698, 801, 968, and the quick pills
already carried the matching `rgba(94,158,255,0.5)` border).

**The `403` console errors are gone; they were a fixture gap, not an app bug.**
`installRetailMocks` was retail-only, but the probes walk `/property`, `/trades`
and settings. `/api/push/preferences` and `/api/subscription` reached the real
dev server with a dummy token. The cross-vertical and settings endpoints are now
mocked in `retail-fixtures.mjs` for every script that uses it, so
`probe-transitions.mjs` no longer patches property/trades in on the side. Match
them **by prefix**: a Playwright glob matches the full URL including its query
string, so an exact pattern misses `/tenants/1`, `/tenants/1/events` and
`/invoices?tenantId=1`. Both probe runs are now free of console errors, and
`/property/tenants/1` renders in ~21ms instead of ~292ms on the 403 error path.

`docs/design/desktop-app/Taptpay Desktop.dc.html`.

## 9. Accepted-change queue — implemented (reviewed 2026-08-06)

All seven items below are implemented. The isolated-Postgres, automated, visual,
mobile-regression, and read-only audit results are recorded in the final QA report.
The descriptions are retained as historical implementation context:

1. **Payment/addressing safety gate.** Complete Phase 0 of
   `docs/PLAN-2026-08-06-payment-links-no-board.md`: allowlisted merchant and
   transaction responses, canonical Postgres board persistence + ownership checks,
   transactionally serialized first-free board allocation, explicit active scopes,
   header-authenticated SSE audiences, redacted logging, and removal of the stale
   MemStorage cache. Run the read-only historical board/null audit; never guess a
   backfill.
2. **Post-fix boundary pass.** Complete Phase 1 of that plan: endpoint chart peaks,
   active property choices/live count, consistent desktop keypad glyphs,
   split-aware trades outstanding totals, readable/accessibly named client rows,
   and settings response-contract coverage.
3. **b4 — Revenue by Board report.** Only start after board persistence is fixed.
   Remove the Fees report from
   `desktop/data/retail-reports.ts` (leaving 9) and add *Revenue by Board*:
   revenue / count / average per board off `transactions.taptStoneId` joined to
   the stones table, with an explicit "Unassigned" bucket. Historical null-board
   data is known to include rows whose board intent was lost; do not present that
   bucket as proven no-board revenue.
4. **b2 — no-board payment links + board creation.** Complete Phases 2–6 of the
   corrected plan. The token must remain the credential through checkout and
   receipt; tokenized rows must be unreachable through numeric public routes.
   Durable payment-attempt/idempotency rows and transactional split setup are
   required before any per-payment link is enabled.
5. **D2 — `ReportModal` into the desktop frame.** It portals to `document.body`
   (`components/reports/ReportModal.tsx:98,259`), so Export covers the browser
   window instead of the simulated 13″ frame. Portal to `.tapt-desktop-frame`
   when present. **Trap:** the frame is inside a `transform: scale(...)` canvas,
   so the modal's `position:fixed; inset:0` must become absolute or it will be
   scale-relative.
6. **D1 — mobile push onto the shared hook.** `hooks/use-push-notifications.ts` is
   used only by `desktop/DesktopSettingsPage.tsx`; `pages/settings.tsx:144-350`
   still carries its own inline copy including the native-iOS branch. Own commit,
   needs real-device testing.
7. **b7 — the two missing notification toggles.** The big one, deliberately last.
   `push_subscriptions` (`shared/schema.ts:573`) has no preference column, and
   `sendPushToMerchant` is called from 13 sites with the type passed at the call
   site, never compared against anything stored. Of the design's three toggles
   only "payment received" maps to something real: there is **no daily-payout job
   at all**, and `sendPushToMerchant` is never called with a `failed` status.
   Needs: preferences column + migration `0012`, filtering inside
   `sendPushToMerchant`, a daily-payout job, and a failed-payment send site.

P5 and P6 followed the queue and are complete in the verified branch state. See
the final QA report before deployment.

# Plan — mobile responsive UI (phone terminal + app-wide)

Date: 2026-08-17
Status: **diagnosis complete and measured; no code changed yet**
Scope: the phone merchant app. Tablet/desktop (`client/src/desktop/**`) is *not* affected
by the primary root cause and is out of scope except where a shared component is extracted.

Everything below was measured in a real browser, not inferred. Method and raw numbers
are in §8. Reproduce with the probes described there.

---

## 0. Summary

Oliver reported five issues. All five reproduce, and **four of them share one root cause**:
a blanket `min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px` applied to *every* `<button>` in the app
below 640px (`client/src/index.css:360-368`). Because `min-height` beats `height`, every
component that sets its own height is silently inflated on phones only — and only on
phones, which is why every existing desktop/tablet probe passes while the phone UI is
visibly broken.

| # | Reported | Root cause | Confirmed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | UI doesn't adapt across sizes; squished, wrong padding | RC-1 + RC-3 + RC-4 + RC-5 | 5–13 inflated buttons on *every* mobile route; 0 uses of `clamp()` in 4 500 lines of terminal UI |
| 2 | Active stack squished, shows 1 of N, needs ≥3 | RC-3 (+RC-1) | 0 rows at 320/375, 1 row at 390/393, 2 rows at 344/412/430. Never 3 on any phone |
| 3 | `$$` figure doesn't shrink when large | RC-4 | `$99999.99` needs 430px at the hardcoded 88px; only 264–374px available. Overflows on *every* phone |
| 4 | Action bar breaks; highlight bubble half height, cuts text | RC-1 + RC-2 | Bubble 27px inside a 44px row (61%); label's bottom sits **4.6px below** the bubble |
| 5 | Split-bill pill changes shape / taller than the action bar | RC-1 | Pill renders 44px against a designed 30px; bar 56px inside its own 37px row; send 44px in a 37px slot |

There is also a latent sixth cause (three unscoped copies of the same global `.tp-*`
stylesheet) that explains the *intermittency* — "keeps breaking" rather than "is broken".

**None of this was caught because the only mobile gate runs at one viewport and never
measures a single internal component.** Fixing the five symptoms without fixing that is
how they come back; §7 is the part that actually prevents recurrence.

---

## 1. Decisions needed from Oliver

These change the shape of the work. The plan below assumes the recommended answer and
is written so a different answer only changes §4 and §5.

**D1 — Adaptation strategy.**
- **(a) Fluid / intrinsic layout — recommended.** Design tokens + `clamp()` + container
  queries + measured chrome gutters. Everything reflows; type stays a readable physical
  size on every device; respects OS text-size settings. Most work, correct result.
- (b) Uniform scaled canvas, the way `client/src/desktop/ScaledCanvas` already works:
  design once at 390×844 and `transform: scale()` to fit. Cheap and pixel-perfect, but
  text becomes physically tiny on a 320px phone and tap targets scale below the 44px
  minimum. Appropriate for the tablet *simulation* of a laptop; wrong for a real phone.
- (c) Hybrid: scale a root design unit with the viewport (clamped), let vertical stacks
  flex. This is what the plan actually implements — (a) with (c)'s type ramp.

**D2 — Smallest supported phone.** The plan assumes **320×568** (iPhone SE 1st gen,
older Android, and iPhone in Display Zoom). If 360×640 is the floor instead, the clamp
minimums relax and §4's "3 rows at 568px tall" stops needing a compact row variant.

**D3 — Blast radius of the RC-1 fix.** Removing the blanket 44px rule changes the
rendered height of 5–13 buttons on *every* mobile page — mostly back toward the original
design. One sweeping commit with a full visual sweep, or page-by-page? Recommend one
commit plus the §7 gate, because a half-applied fix leaves two inconsistent button
systems live at once.

**D4 — Money formatting.** `fmt()` produces `$99999.99` with no thousands separator.
Should it be `$99,999.99`? Grouping *widens* the string, so the fitter in §5 must be
sized for whichever is chosen. Current maximum is 7 digits (`digits.length < 7`).

---

## 2. Root causes

### RC-1 — A blanket 44px minimum on every button below 640px  ⟵ *the primary cause*

`client/src/index.css:360-368`:

```css
@media (max-width: 640px) {
  button, [role="button"], input[type="submit"], input[type="button"] {
    min-height: 44px;
    min-width: 44px;
  }
}
```

`min-height` wins over `height`, so no component can set a smaller box without
`!important`. Measured consequences (iPhone 14, 390×844):

| Element | Author intent | Rendered | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.tp-subbar-btn` | `height: 27px` | **44px** | +17 |
| `.tp-subbar-ind` (a `<div>`, so unaffected) | 27px | 27px | — |
| `.tp-subbar` (bar shell) | 5+27+5+2 = 39px | **56px** | +17 |
| `.tp-psubbar` (the row it lives in, a `<div>`) | 37px | 37px | — |
| `.tp-send` | `height: 37px` | **44px** | +7 |
| `.tp-pill` "split bill" | ~30px | **44px** | +14 |
| `.tp-pill` "paywave"/"boards" | ~26px | **44px** | +18 |
| `.tp-stack-hdr` (sized by its chevron button) | 24px | **44px** | +20 |
| `.tp-stepper` (quantity) | `32×32` | **44×44** | +12 |

So the action bar is a 56px lozenge inside a 37px row, holding a 27px highlight bubble
behind a label that is centred in a 44px box. A/B proof: disabling only these two
declarations at runtime takes the stack header from **44px → 24px** with nothing else
changed (§8.4).

Two secondary effects worth knowing:
- It is a `max-width: 640px` query, so tablet/desktop never see it. Every probe in
  `scripts/desktop-shots/` runs at ≥1194px. The bug is invisible to the entire existing
  test suite by construction.
- `min-width: 44px` also inflates narrow controls — the quantity steppers, the share
  icons, the stack chevron.

**The rest of that media block is also load-bearing damage.** Lines 360–473 are a legacy
"dark glass" override set that now applies to every modern mobile page:

```css
label  { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.95) !important; }   /* white labels on light panels */
input  { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08) !important;
         border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.20) !important;
         color: black !important; }                    /* overrides .tp-field entirely */
table, tbody, thead, tr, td, th { background: transparent !important; }
.backdrop-blur-xl, .backdrop-blur-sm { background/border !important; }
```

These are not the reported bugs, but they are the same failure mode and they will keep
producing "padding is not correct" reports. Treat the block as one unit (§3.1).

### RC-2 — The highlight bubble is half-measured, half-hardcoded, and never re-measured

`RetailTerminalViewCore.jsx:89-109`. `measure()` returns `{ x, w }` only; `top: 5px` and
`height: 27px` live in CSS. The bubble is therefore *guaranteed* to be wrong the moment a
button's real height differs from 27px — which RC-1 makes permanent.

Second defect in the same hook: the effect depends on `[activeIdx]` with no
`ResizeObserver` and no `resize` listener. Measured drift after resizing 390 → 320 with
"split" active: the bubble ends up **14.5px off-centre from its button** and stays there
(§8.5). On a real phone that fires on rotation, on the software keyboard opening, and on
the iOS URL bar collapsing.

`TerminalDockView.tsx:98-118` has the identical pattern; it survives only because its
track width is pinned at 280px.

### RC-3 — Layout is absolute-pixel choreography around floating chrome

`MainTerminal` / `PendingTerminal` (`RetailTerminalViewCore.jsx:318-374`):

```jsx
<div style={{ height: '50%', padding: '100px 28px 28px' }}>   {/* hero  */}
<div style={{ flex: 1,      padding: '154px 22px 90px'  }}>   {/* stack */}
```

`154px` is a guess at the footprint of the floating FAB + action bar; `90px` is a guess
at the dock's. Nothing measures either. The dock is 78px tall and **collapses to 44px
after 4 seconds of idle** — the padding never reacts. There are **28** `height: '50%'`
panels across the three terminal views.

The arithmetic, measured (row height 69px, header 44px, card border 2px — 3 rows needs
**245px** of content box):

| Device | lower panel | content box (−244 padding) | rows fully visible |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320×568 | 284 | **40** | **0** |
| 375×667 | 333 | **89** | **0** |
| 390×844 | 422 | 178 | **1** |
| 393×851 | 425 | 181 | **1** |
| 344×882 | 441 | 197 | 2 |
| 412×915 | 457 | 213 | 2 |
| 430×932 | 466 | 222 | 2 |

The requirement "at least 3" is not reachable on **any** phone without changing the
structure. Note the stack header lives *inside* the scroll container, so it also consumes
first-paint budget and then scrolls away.

### RC-4 — No fluid type, no intrinsic sizing, anywhere

Census of the three terminal views:

| | retail | property | trades |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fontSize: <number>` literals | 66 | 104 | 58 |
| `height: '50%'` panels | 9 | 11 | 8 |
| `clamp()` / `min()` / `max()` / `cq*` | **0** | **0** | **0** |

Plus 194 hardcoded `px` values in the retail CSS template literal.

The amount is `fontSize: 88` at ten call sites (76 at one). Measured widths of
`$99999.99` at 88px Outfit 900 vs the space available:

| Device | text needs | space | overflow |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320×568 | 430px | 264px | **+166** |
| 375×667 | 430px | 319px | **+111** |
| 390×844 | 430px | 334px | **+96** |
| 430×932 | 430px | 374px | **+56** |

It clips on the largest phone made. On 320 the wrap pushes the hero block to `y: -162`
and the split-bill pill to `y: -78` — **both entirely above the top of the screen** — and
the keypad's top row is left half-hidden behind the action bar.

### RC-5 — Wrong viewport unit, no safe areas

`.tp-viewport` in the retail terminal uses `height: 100vh`. Every other mobile surface in
the app (`property`, `trades`, `transactions`, `settings`, `stock-management`) uses
`100svh`. On iOS Safari `100vh` is the *large* viewport, so with the URL bar showing the
terminal is ~60–100px taller than the visible area — the bottom of the active stack and
the dock fall below the fold, on top of RC-3's squeeze.

`viewport-fit=cover` is set in `client/index.html:5`, so `env(safe-area-inset-*)` is
available — but the terminal uses none of it. The notch is cleared by a hardcoded
`padding-top: 100px` (hero) and `52px` (top banner, subhead is `20px` and sits under the
status bar); the home indicator is not cleared at all. Only `TerminalDockView` and
`notification-system` use safe-area insets today.

### RC-6 — Three unscoped copies of the same `.tp-*` global stylesheet (the intermittency)

- `RetailTerminalViewCore.jsx:1451` injects `TP_CSS` — **unscoped** global `.tp-*` rules.
- `PropertyTerminalView.tsx:1339` injects `TP_TERM_CSS` — **unscoped**, same selectors,
  *different values*: `.tp-subbar { transform: scale(0.85) }`, `.tp-subbar-btn { padding: 0 22px }`,
  and `.tp-subbar-ind { z-index: 2 }` — which paints the navy bubble **over** the label
  rather than behind it.
- `trades-terminal-view.css` is correctly scoped under `.trades-terminal-view`.

Measured on `/property/terminal`: **two `<style>` tags defining `.tp-subbar` are live at
once**, and the retail-shaped bar renders at `matrix(0.85, …)`, 241×48 instead of 316×56.
Whichever `<style>` is later in the DOM wins. Routes are usually exclusive so the window
is short, but it opens on every cross-vertical transition and whenever two terminal views
mount together (the landing phone demo). This is the difference between "is broken" and
"keeps breaking".

### RC-7 — The only mobile gate proves nothing about layout

`scripts/verify-mobile-retail-regression.mjs` runs **one** viewport (390×844) and asserts
the *outer* box is 390×844 with `scrollWidth === 390`, plus API-contract checks. It passes
today, against the screenshots in §8. It never measures an internal component, never
changes size, never rotates, and never simulates a safe area.

---

## 3. Phase 1 — remove RC-1 without losing touch accessibility

The 44px rule exists for a real reason (Apple HIG minimum tap target; WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8
requires 24×24 CSS px). Deleting it outright regresses accessibility. Give the hit area
back **without touching the layout box**:

```css
/* client/src/styles/tap-target.css */
.tap-target { position: relative; }
.tap-target::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  left: 50%; top: 50%;
  transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
  width:  max(100%, 44px);
  height: max(100%, 44px);
  /* no background; extends the hit region only */
}
```

A pseudo-element is part of its originating element for hit-testing, so the tap region
grows while the painted box, the flex/grid contribution, and every sibling's position stay
exactly as designed.

### 3.1 Steps

1. Delete `min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px` from `client/src/index.css:362-368`.
   **Keep** the `input … { font-size: 16px }` rule at :371-379 (it prevents the iOS focus
   zoom) but split it out so it no longer carries `min-height`.
2. Add `.tap-target` to the controls that are now smaller than 44px: `.tp-subbar-btn`,
   the active-stack chevron, `.tp-stepper` at its 32px call sites, `.tp-share-btn`,
   `.tp-qr-expand`, `.tp-qr-modal-close`, and the equivalents in property/trades.
   Everything already ≥44px needs nothing.
3. Audit the rest of the `@media (max-width: 640px)` block (lines 360–473) as one unit.
   Each `!important` override is either (a) still needed by a specific legacy page — move
   it behind a `.legacy-glass` class on that page's root, or (b) dead — delete it. The
   `label`, `input`, `table`, and `.backdrop-blur-*` overrides are the ones that will keep
   producing "padding is wrong" reports on new pages.
4. Run the §7 gate and a full visual sweep before committing. Expect *every* mobile page
   to change; that is the point, and it is why D3 matters.

### 3.2 Expected effect on the reported issues

Issue 4's bubble goes from 27-in-44 to 27-in-27 (correct by accident — §5 makes it correct
by construction). Issue 5's pill returns to 30px and the bar to 39px. Issue 2 recovers 20px
of stack budget. Issue 1 improves on every route. Issue 3 is untouched — that is RC-4.

---

## 4. Phase 2 — the responsive foundation

### 4.1 One token layer

New `client/src/styles/mobile-tokens.css`, applied at the phone app root:

```css
.tp-viewport {
  container-type: inline-size;          /* size off our own 430px-capped box, not the window */

  /* the design ratio: 1.0 at the 390px reference, clamped so 320 and 430 stay sane */
  --u: clamp(0.84, calc(100cqi / 390), 1.10);

  --sp-1: calc(4px  * var(--u));  --sp-2: calc(8px  * var(--u));
  --sp-3: calc(12px * var(--u));  --sp-4: calc(16px * var(--u));
  --sp-6: calc(24px * var(--u));  --sp-7: calc(28px * var(--u));

  --safe-top:    env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px);
  --safe-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px);

  --bar-h:  calc(38px * var(--u));   /* the action bar's *only* height source */
  --row-h:  calc(64px * var(--u));   /* one active-stack row */

  height: 100vh;      /* fallback order matters */
  height: 100svh;
  height: 100dvh;
}
```

Container queries (`cqi`, `container-type`) are Baseline since Safari 16 / Chrome 105 and
need no build support — Vite 5 + Tailwind 3.4 pass them through untouched. Using `cqi`
rather than `vw` is what makes the same components correct inside the landing page's
phone demo and on a tablet, not only in a full-window phone.

### 4.2 Rules that replace the current habits

| Instead of | Use |
|---|---|
| `fontSize: 88` | `font-size: clamp(<floor>, <fluid cqi>, <ceiling>)` from the type ramp |
| `padding: '154px 22px 90px'` | grid rows + measured gutters (§5.2) |
| `height: '50%'` | `grid-template-rows` with `minmax()` |
| `height: 100vh` | the `svh`/`dvh` chain above |
| hardcoded notch/home-indicator clearance | `var(--safe-top)` / `var(--safe-bottom)` |
| a hardcoded `height` on any flex child | a token, and `min-height: 0` on the scroll parent |

Every fixed dimension gets a `clamp()` whose floor still works at **320×568** (per D2).

---

## 5. Phase 3–5 — the three reported components

### 5.1 Phase 3 — the action bar (issues 4 and 5)

Extract one `SegmentedBar` component (`client/src/features/terminal/shared/`) and use it
from all three verticals — this also removes three divergent copies of the same bug.

**Make the bubble unable to diverge, rather than measuring it more carefully.** Put the
buttons and the indicator in the same CSS grid and let the grid place it:

```css
.tp-bar        { display: grid; grid-auto-flow: column; align-items: stretch;
                 height: var(--bar-h); padding: var(--sp-1); }
.tp-bar-ind    { grid-row: 1; grid-column: var(--active-col);
                 transition: grid-column 0s, transform .45s var(--ease-bar); }
.tp-bar-btn    { grid-row: 1; height: 100%; }   /* stretch — never a fixed px height */
```

The indicator now shares the row track with the buttons, so its height *is* the button
height, always, whatever RC-1-shaped rule appears in future. Keep the JS measurement only
for the sliding `transform` between columns, and add:

- a `ResizeObserver` on the track and on each button,
- a `document.fonts.ready` re-measure (label widths change when Outfit loads),
- the same treatment for `TerminalDockView`'s indicator.

**Invariants the gate enforces** (§7):

1. `bar.height === var(--bar-h)`, independent of button count, labels, or compact state.
2. `indicator.height === activeButton.height` and the active label's box is fully inside
   the indicator's box (top and bottom gap both ≥ 0).
3. `sendButton.height === bar.height` and `splitPill.height === bar.height`.
4. `bar.scrollWidth <= bar.clientWidth` — the bar is never clipped.
5. The whole row fits inside the viewport with a gutter at 320px wide.
6. After a viewport change, (2) still holds — this is the RC-2 regression test.

**Morphing.** The compact ⇄ expanded transition currently animates `padding` while the
label pops in at full width, which is what reads as "breaking". Animate the label's track
(`grid-template-columns: … 0fr → 1fr`, or a `max-width` on `.tp-bar-label`) so the bar's
width change is continuous, and keep the same `--ease-bar` for the indicator and the width
so they arrive together.

**Split-bill pill.** Its height becomes `var(--bar-h)` — the same token as the bar, so
"exact height of the action bar" is enforced by construction, not by two numbers that
happen to match. The row it participates in reserves its width the same way the send slot
does, so the bar morphs to make room instead of the pill overlapping it.

### 5.2 Phase 4 — terminal home layout (issue 2)

Replace `height: 50%` + magic padding with an explicit three-row grid:

```css
.tp-screen {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows:
    minmax(var(--hero-min), var(--hero-pref))            /* hero  */
    var(--chrome-gutter)                                 /* the floating FAB / bar band */
    minmax(var(--stack-min), 1fr);                       /* stack */
  padding-bottom: calc(var(--dock-h) + var(--safe-bottom) + var(--sp-3));
}
```

- `--chrome-gutter` is **measured** from the overlay that is actually visible (FAB when
  shown, otherwise the bar) by a `ResizeObserver`, and written to the root as a custom
  property. It can never be a stale `154px` again.
- `--dock-h` is measured from `TerminalDockView` the same way — it collapses 58px → 44px
  after 4s of idle and today nothing reacts.
- `--stack-min: calc(3 * var(--row-h) + var(--stack-hdr-h) + 2px)` makes **"at least 3
  rows" a CSS invariant**, not an outcome.
- Move `.tp-stack-hdr` **out** of `.tp-stack-scroll` so it pins and the three rows are
  three *content* rows.

Budget check at 390×844 — the stack needs 245px and has 178px, so 67px must come back:
header out of the scroll (+24 to the scroll's usable height), gutter 154 → ~110 (+44),
bottom padding 90 → measured ~86 (+4), hero 422 → ~400 (+22). Comfortably feasible.

At **320×568** (D2) the arithmetic is tighter: dock 78 + hero floor 240 leaves ~250px, and
three rows plus a header need ~243px. It fits, but only if the hero contracts first and
the amount clamps with it. If Oliver wants headroom there, add a compact row variant below
~600px of height (status word → dot + chip) — flag as a design call, do not invent it.

Ordering rule for short screens: **the stack floor is non-negotiable; the hero contracts
first**, and the amount's `clamp()` ceiling is tied to the hero's realised height.

### 5.3 Phase 5 — the money display (issue 3)

The requirement is "cut off on space, then the font shrinks". Two layers:

1. **Normal case, no JS.** `white-space: nowrap` plus a width-aware size:

   ```css
   .tp-amount {
     white-space: nowrap;
     font-size: min(
       var(--amount-max),                                   /* the 88px design ceiling */
       calc(100cqi / var(--amount-chars) * var(--amount-k))  /* fit to the character count */
     );
   }
   ```

   React sets `--amount-chars` from the formatted string's length. Deterministic, no
   measurement, no reflow loop, and trivially assertable in a test. `--amount-k` is a
   single constant calibrated once against the Outfit 900 advance width.

2. **Fallback for the long case / late font load.** A small `useFitText` hook comparing
   `scrollWidth` to `clientWidth` on `[text, boxWidth, fontsReady]`, writing a `--fit`
   scale with a floor (~0.55 of base). Below the floor, switch to a compact presentation
   rather than shrinking into illegibility.

Apply to **all ten** `.tp-amount` call sites in retail plus the property/trades
equivalents — each currently hardcodes `fontSize: 88` (or `76`).

Also fix the containers: `.tp-screen` and `.tp-layer` are `overflow: hidden`, which is
what turns an overflow into a silent clip. Once the amount is fitted they stay hidden, but
the gate must assert the amount's box is inside its parent rather than trusting the clip.

Related, pending D4: `fmt()` has no thousands separator. If grouping is added the string
gets wider and `--amount-k` must be recalibrated.

---

## 6. Phase 6 — scope the CSS and de-duplicate (RC-6)

1. Scope `TP_CSS` under `.retail-terminal-view` and `TP_TERM_CSS` under
   `.property-terminal-view`, exactly as `trades-terminal-view.css` already does.
2. Better: move all three out of template literals into real `.css` files so Vite dedupes
   them, they are cacheable, and they stop being re-parsed on every mount.
3. Then extract the genuinely shared primitives — bar, amount, stack row, pill, field,
   CTA, dot — into one `terminal-primitives.css` driven by the §4.1 tokens, so the next
   fix lands once instead of three times.

Note for whoever does this: the handoff (`docs/HANDOFF-2026-07-28-tablet-desktop-app.md`
§6) records that Oliver **accepted** the duplication of the *home-screen* furniture on
desktop. That ruling was about desktop home screens; it does not cover these three
unscoped global stylesheets colliding on the phone, which is a correctness bug, not a
duplication preference. Raise it if in doubt — do not silently reverse a ruling.

---

## 7. Phase 7 — the gates that stop this recurring

This is the part that matters most. Without it the five symptoms return the next time
someone adds a global rule.

### 7.1 `scripts/verify-mobile-responsive.mjs`

For each viewport in **{320×568, 360×640, 375×667, 390×844, 412×915, 430×932}**, each
mobile route, and both orientations:

1. `document.scrollWidth === clientWidth` (no horizontal scroll).
2. No visible element's box crosses the viewport edge, with an explicit allowlist for
   deliberately-clipped elements (e.g. the collapsed `.tp-send-slot`).
3. No text node clipped: `scrollWidth <= clientWidth + 2` for every leaf with text.
4. **Component contracts** — the invariants in §5.1, plus:
   `visibleStackRows >= 3`; the amount's box inside its parent at `$99,999.99`.
5. **Re-measure after `setViewportSize`** — this is the RC-2 drift test and the one that
   would have caught the 14.5px bubble offset.
6. Run once with a simulated safe-area inset and once with the dock collapsed.

Model it on `scripts/desktop-shots/probe-terminal-geometry.mjs`, which already proves the
"measure, don't look" pattern works. Use `retail-fixtures.mjs` for auth and mocks. **Exit
non-zero on failure** — several existing scripts collect errors and still exit 0.

### 7.2 Static guards (cheap, catch the cause not the symptom)

- CI grep: no `min-height`/`min-width` in a bare *element* selector inside a media query
  in `client/src/**/*.css`. This is the rule that would have blocked RC-1 at review.
- CI grep: no new `fontSize: <number>` literals or `height: '50%'` under
  `client/src/features/terminal/**`.
- CI grep: no `height: 100vh` in phone surfaces — `svh`/`dvh` only.
- CI grep: no unscoped `.tp-` selector in a `<style>` template literal.

### 7.3 Process

- Wire `verify-mobile-responsive.mjs` into the same place `verify-desktop-p0.mjs` runs, so
  "phone" is a first-class gate rather than a manual check.
- Record the six device classes in `CLAUDE.md` next to the existing desktop/tablet
  definitions, so the next agent tests all of them by default.

---

## 8. Evidence

Dev server on `:5000` (single instance — memory `dev-server-single-instance`), nix
Chromium at `/nix/store/zi4f80l169xlmivz8vja8wlphq74qqk0-chromium-125.0.6422.141/bin/chromium`
(memory `playwright-nix-chromium`), auth and API via `scripts/desktop-shots/retail-fixtures.mjs`
with `hasTouch: true, isMobile: true`. Probe sources and raw JSON are in this session's
scratchpad; they are the starting point for §7.1.

**8.1 Stack rows visible** — 7 transactions in the fixture, row height 69px:
0 rows at 320×568 and 375×667; 1 at 390×844 and 393×851; 2 at 344×882, 412×915, 430×932.

**8.2 Action bar, iPhone 14** — `.tp-subbar-btn` computed `44px` (CSS: 27px);
`.tp-subbar-ind` `27px`; `.tp-subbar` box `316×56`; `.tp-psubbar` `37px` → the bar
overflows its own row by **19px**; `.tp-send` `44px` in a `37px` slot. With "split" active:
`labelInsideInd = { topGap: 12.4, bottomGap: -4.6 }` — **the label's bottom edge is 4.6px
below the bottom of the bubble.**

**8.3 Amount** — `$99999.99` at 88px measures **430px**; available 264 / 319 / 334 / 374px
at 320 / 375 / 390 / 430. At 320 the hero lands at `y: -162` and the split pill at `y: -78`.

**8.4 RC-1 A/B** — removing only `min-height`/`min-width` from the 640px block at runtime:
`.tp-stack-hdr` 44px → **24px**, its button 44×44 → **24×32**. Nothing else changed.

**8.5 RC-2 drift** — with "split" active, resizing 390 → 320: bubble centre vs active
button centre goes from **1px** to **14.5px** and stays. The dock indicator holds (its
track is a fixed 280px).

**8.6 RC-6 collision** — on `/property/terminal`, two `<style>` tags define `.tp-subbar`;
the computed transform is `matrix(0.85, 0, 0, 0.85, 0, 0)` and `.tp-subbar-ind` computes
`z-index: 2` (over the label) instead of retail's `0` (behind it).

**8.7 App-wide inflation** — buttons pinned to exactly 44px per route:
`/terminal` 13, `/property/terminal` 12, `/property` 10, `/trades` 10, `/dashboard` 9,
`/stock` 9, `/transactions` 9, `/settings` 9, `/trades/terminal` 5. Identical at 320, 390
and 430, i.e. it is not a small-screen edge case — it is every phone.

---

## 9. Execution order

| Phase | Content | Gate before commit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Land §7.1 as a **failing** baseline; record current numbers | probe runs, reports failures |
| 1 | RC-1: remove the blanket rule, add `.tap-target`, audit the 640px block | §7.1 + full visual sweep (D3) |
| 2 | §4 token layer, `svh`/`dvh`, safe areas | §7.1 clauses 1–3 pass |
| 3 | `SegmentedBar` + grid indicator + observers (issues 4, 5) | §5.1 invariants 1–6 pass |
| 4 | Terminal home grid + measured gutters (issue 2) | `visibleStackRows >= 3` on all six sizes |
| 5 | Amount fitting (issue 3) | amount inside its parent at max value, all six sizes |
| 6 | Scope + de-duplicate the three stylesheets | §7.2 greps clean; no `.tp-` leakage |
| 7 | Wire the gate into CI, update `CLAUDE.md` | full suite green |

Stop conditions: do not start Phase 3 before Phase 1 lands (the invariants cannot hold
while RC-1 is live), and do not start Phase 4 before Phase 2 (the grid needs the tokens).
Phases 5 and 6 are independent of each other.

Regression boundaries that must stay green throughout: the tablet/desktop app
(`scripts/desktop-shots/*`, `scripts/verify-desktop-p0.mjs`), the landing phone demo, and
the public customer routes.
